answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-bound identity: each agent locks a bond at a staking wharf before a haven registry issues one credential, so k identities require k distinct bonds. Auditor falcon agents randomly sample credentials and confirm each bond is real and unique; forged or reused bonds get slashed. An attacker posing as k honest nodes must commit k times the bond up front, and with audit probability p each fake identity risks forfeiting it, so expected cost is k times bond times p plus locked capital. Fake identity costs real money, not just a keypair.
